title: An Agent's irreversible disabling of token emissions can still be reverted by Sky Governance under the Risk Framework
content:
A.2.2.5.4.2.7 requires the Agent Token Primitive to state whether emissions beyond current supply have been irreversibly disabled, and then qualifies the word 'irreversibly': "Once Disabled is set to `True`, the action cannot be undone **by the Agent**. Sky Governance retains the ability to revert the Disabled setting where the Agent is in violation of Risk Capital requirements and emissions are required by the Risk Framework."

The asymmetry is the claim. An Agent's strongest possible promise to its token holders — that their stake can never be diluted — is unilateral and one-directional. It removes the Agent's own optionality without removing Sky's. Holders relying on a hard supply cap are relying on a cap with a named exception they do not control.

The justification is coherent from the ecosystem's side: emissions are a recapitalization tool. If an Agent breaches Risk Capital requirements, diluting existing holders may be the only way to restore solvency, and an Agent that had locked emissions could otherwise render itself unrescuable. This is the same reasoning as the ban on deactivating the Root Edit Primitive (A.2.2.1.2.4.2.1.2) — the Atlas systematically refuses to let Agents destroy the mechanisms needed to fix them.

The cost is credibility. A supply cap that a third party can lift on a condition the holder cannot verify in advance is a weaker commitment than the word "irreversibly" suggests, and the exception's trigger — the Risk Framework — is defined outside this document.
description: Once set to True the Agent can never undo it, but Sky retains the power to re-enable emissions where the Agent breaches Risk Capital requirements — so the commitment binds only one party.
